requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap in how the reviewed tests check `requirements.authoring.invocation`. I reviewed only the supplied test sources and did not request any implementation source.

The cited `requirements.authoring.refresh` and `requirements.authoring.reassessment` are context only. Their own tests are not reassessed here.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Command form and options.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` runs `author <subject> --config alternate --force`. It asserts that the alternate profile's model, key and backend are used.
  - `-v` and `--verbose` are exercised in `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]`. They are also exercised, together with `--stdout`, in `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]`.
  - `--missing`, `--force` and `--stdout` are exercised in `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]`. That test also covers the refresh rule that `--missing` and `--force` are mutually exclusive, and that `--stdout` cannot be combined with `--missing`.

- **Selecting one existing requirement or named example in the current project.**
  - `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs both a requirement subject and an example subject (`requirements.ready_case`). It checks the evidence record kind and the "Subject: <kind> <name>" message for each.
  - `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` asserts that an unknown name fails with the name in stderr and that the evidence file is left unchanged.
  - `fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` runs from a nested directory of the project.

- **Completion report content.**
  - `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that stdout starts with `<subject>: ollama / <model>`. It also asserts an `Evidence:` line whose path resolves to `evidence/<subject>.json`, and a `Usage:` line.
  - `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` repeats the subject, backend and model check. It asserts the evidence path equals the project evidence file and that the usage path is an existing file.

- **Evidence destination by default and with `--stdout`.**
  - The default is covered by the evidence path assertions above.
  - In `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]`, stdout parses as JSON evidence. Stderr contains the subject, backend and model line, `Evidence: stdout`, and a `Usage:` path that is an existing file. The test runs both with and without an existing evidence directory, with true, false and FIXME determinations, and with and without verbose.

- **Stdout mode sends the report and diagnostics to stderr.**
  - The stdout test asserts that the report is on stderr and that stdout holds only the JSON evidence.
  - `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` asserts that stdout is empty when a `--stdout` run fails, so diagnostics did not go to stdout. It also asserts the evidence file is unchanged.

- **`author-evidence` is an alias for the single-subject command.** It is used in the ollama CLI test, the stdout test, the failed-submission test, and the current-record case in the batch test. In that last case it produces the same output as `author`.

The `Fixture` struct and its `run` and `command` helpers carry the {test} reference and are reached from the marked tests. All marked tests carry {test} references to this requirement, so there is no marking gap.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST initially assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current on initial selection.
After that selection, {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment` governs each round. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reassessment
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
